chunk_map.heading: Painting the picture with the LLM
Two frontiers: how fast, and the right things

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 1 "The LLM mirrors your stance": line 9: "The LLM is the infinite version of it: your stance as input to the session is mirrored in the output." — closest near-miss: "it" reads back to "the taste behind the tool" (line 9, same sentence pair) and "that argument" (Godin's), both inside chunk 1, so it resolves within the same chunk. Every other pronoun/demonstrative ("It will be what fits the session" line 7, "It was trained to match you" line 11, "You prime the context. The LLM scales it." line 16, "that setup" line 24) binds to an antecedent named earlier in the same chunk or the immediately preceding chunk's carried vocabulary ("the LLM", "your setup"/"you prime"). No forward reference, no cross-file pointer.

rules_evaluated.na_reason: no pointers to other files by position anywhere in the body; Godin is named-only, no location claim.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: file is the opener of M1 (maintainer Meta block: "Role: opener. First lecture of M1"); body contains no backward-pointing "the X you did/saw" reference to any prior beat.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.na_reason: no guess-before-reveal structure in this file; maintainer's own delivery watch-for (L96) confirms the two frontier questions are deliberately left unanswered rather than staged as a reveal.

rules_evaluated.evidence: Each of the three `##` chunks (1, 2, 3) carries 4-6 full sentences of standalone claim content — none is a single wait-state bullet or a context-dependent fragment. Chunk 0 is the plain H1 title, the template's own prior-context slide, not a content chunk to test against this rule.

chunk 1 header "The LLM mirrors your stance" is restated verbatim as the chunk's closing line (line 7). chunk 2 header "You prime, the LLM scales" is restated near-verbatim at line 16 ("You prime the context. The LLM scales it."). chunk 3 header "Two frontiers: how fast, and the right things" names exactly the two questions the chunk poses (line 24 "can that setup learn faster than you can write things down?"; line 26 "does it learn the right things"). No header the chunk's own content contradicts.

Closest specimen: chunk 2 line 20 "If you want a shotgun, you have a shotgun. If you want a cannon, you have that too." — a two-leg parallel construction, not the banned "Not X. Not Y. Z." shape and not a three-leg anaphora/epistrophe triple, and explicitly maintainer-attested as a deliberate provocation beat to keep (L35, L43 accept-notes). No self-grading superlative, no number-with-retraction (no numbers in body), no abstraction-noun stack ("high-end engineering skill", "the ceiling" are concrete-enough register, not repo jargon stacks), no verb triplet with an empty leg anywhere in the body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 1 "The LLM mirrors your stance" and chunk 2 "You prime, the LLM scales" are both declarative claims, matching lecture-heading grammar. chunk 3 "Two frontiers: how fast, and the right things" is a catalogue-style heading naming its subject (parallel to the rule's own allowed examples "Ralph", "The numbers") rather than an assertion needing proof, and its content (lines 24, 26) explicitly poses two open questions without answering them — matching the maintainer's own delivery watch-for (L96: "do NOT answer them"). No label-shaped heading is doing claim-work it can't support.
